CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  DESIGN REVIEW BOARD | MINUTES
  REGULAR MEETING – 7:30 P.M.
  City Hall Conference Room A
  111 South First Street

November 14, 2023

A. CALL MEETING TO ORDER: 7:30 P.M.

B. ROLL CALL:

Present:
ANKIT UDANI, CHAIRMAN
NORA HERNANDEZ, VICE CHAIRMAN
STANLEY TSAI, MEMBER
MICHAEL DANINGER, MEMBER
JENNIFER NG, MEMBER
STEVE KUCHENSKI, SECRETARY

C. DRB TRAINING:

At the start of the November 14, 2023, Design Review Board (DRB) routine meeting, the
City Attorney’s office will conduct a DRB training session for all board members which
will discuss topics such as DRB’s role and responsibilities and how those rules relate to
the Brown Act for open meetings for local legislative bodies in California.

ITEM 1:  DRB TRAINING: November 14, 2023

D. CONSENT CALENDAR:

All items listed under Consent Calendar are considered by the Design Review Board to
be routine and will be enacted by one motion unless a citizen or Board Member requests
otherwise; in which case, the item will be removed for separate consideration.

ITEM 2:  MINUTES: October 24, 2023
Recommended Action: Design Review Board review and approve as submitted the
minutes of the October 24, 2023 regular meeting of the Design Review Board.

MOTION:
  • Vice Chairman Hernandez moved to approve all consent items.
  • The second was by Board Member Daninger.
  • The motion carried with the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Udani, Hernandez, Tsai, Daninger, Ng
  Noes:  None

  1
 E. DISCUSSION ITEMS:

ITEM 3:  106 East Linda Vista Avenue

  •  This is an application for a new 3 ft. and 6 ft. high block wall located along the
  east and west property lines and a 3 ft. high wrought iron fence at the front of the
  property facing East Linda Vista Avenue on an existing 1-story single-family
  property.
  •  Applicant: Calvin Quach
  •  Recommended Action: APPROVAL WITH CONDITIONS - The proposed project
  is approved with conditions of approval.
  •  Discussion: Applicant Calvin Quach was not present. Public comment was
  provided by neighboring property owner. Member of the public spoke about the
  proposed wall encroaching on to their property and as a result disrupting and
  damaging their property. With this new insight, Staff recommends for the
  applicant to revise the drawings to graphically depict the proposed wall within the
  property line boundaries or to obtain a shared wall written agreement with the
  owner to build a shared wall and show graphically on the plans. Chairman Udani
  asks if this will impact the design. Staff does not believe this will impact the
  design and notes this is more for clarification. Hernandez notes that there should
  be a section of the proposed wall to better understand the placement of the wall
  is being proposed. Hernandez asks the member of the public if the applicant or
  surveyor shared survey documents with them. The member of the public
  responded no. Secretary Kuchenski notes that the board members can only
  approve walls within the boundaries of the property being reviewed. Board member
  Ng notes that the 3 foot block wall is too massive in comparison to what is seen in
  the surrounding front yards in the neighborhood. Ng would like to see a barrier that
  is less massive and open.

MOTION:

  •  Hernandez makes a motion to approve the application with the following
  conditions: 1) The applicant shall identify the proposed color of the wrought iron
  fence on the plans; 2) Revise the fence elevation to show the height dimension of
  the post measured from grade level to the top of post and shall not exceed 3 feet
  in height; 3) The applicant shall identify the proposed color and/or finish of the
  block walls on the plans; 4) Revise the plans to clearly show the placement of the
  proposed block walls and fence in reference to the property line. Note, if the
  applicant is proposing a block wall and/or fence on a shared property line, then a
  shared wall agreement with the adjacent property owner(s) must be obtained
  prior to any construction; 5) The applicant shall remove the 3 foot high block wall
  and continue the proposed fencing instead, within the front yard setback; and 6)
  The applicant shall resubmit a revised set of drawings for the City Architect to
  verify and approve.
  •  The second was by Board Member Daninger.
  •  The motion carried with the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Udani, Hernandez, Tsai, Daninger, Ng
  Noes:  None

  2
 ITEM 4:  215 South Granada Avenue

  •  This is an application for a new 3-foot-high vinyl picket fence and gate along the
  front yard of an existing 1-story single-family residential property. The project
  includes removing the existing wood style picket fence and installing 58 feet of
  line of an existing 1-story single-family residential property.
  •  Applicant: Stephanie Flores & Porfirio Andrades
  •  Recommended Action: APPROVAL - The proposed project is approved without
  conditions.
  •  Discussion: Property owners were present. Board Member Hernandez
  mentioned that the shiny vinyl is unappealing and is easily stained. Hernandez
  asks that the fence elevation shows the height dimension measured from grade
  to the top of fence. Daninger notes that the surrounding neighborhood does
  consist of white picket fences similar to the proposed project. Hernandez
  requested the applicant propose a different material such as composite wood.
  Daninger agrees that composite material will be more durable. The applicant
  notes that maintenance and cost are the factors for vinyl fence selection.
  Hernandez and Udani note that composite material will help with reducing the
  maintenance burden while providing a high quality material.

MOTION:

  •  Board Member Hernandez makes a motion to approve the application with the
  following conditions: 1) The applicant must select a fencing material of composite
  wood or similar and should avoid the use of low quality vinyl materials; 2) Revise
  the fence elevation to show the maximum height the proposed fence measured
  from grade to the highest point of the fence; 3) The applicant shall identify the
  picket and post top style; and 4) The applicant shall resubmit a revised set of
  drawings for the City Architect to verify and approve.
  •  The second was by Board Member Ng.
  •  The motion carried with the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Udani, Hernandez, Tsai, Daninger, Ng
  Noes:  None

ITEM 5:  1427 West Valley Boulevard

  •  This is an application for exterior improvement to an existing 1- and 2-story multi-
  tenant commercial building, such as re-painting stucco walls, existing window and
  storefront trim, and roof crown molding; as well as refurbish storefront awnings.
  •  Applicant: Yu Li
  •  Recommended Action: APPROVAL - The proposed project is approved without
  conditions.
  •  Discussion: Applicant Yu Li was not present. Board Member Udani asked if the
  applicant was present and requested that the meeting continue.

MOTION:

  •  Udani advised to continue the application since the applicant was not present.
  •  All board members agreed.

  3
   •  No official motion was carried. The project was unofficially continued to the next
  DRB meeting to review and determine a recommended action at the time the
  DRB was adjourned.

ITEM 6:  951 South Meridian Avenue

  •  This is an application for a new 3-foot-high iron fence over an existing low wall, 6-
  foot-high iron fence, and two (2) vehicular gates along the east edge of the multi-
  tenant commercial property fronting South Meridian Avenue.
  •  Applicant: Cindy Li
  •  Recommended Action: APPROVAL - The proposed project is approved without
  conditions.
  •  Discussion: Applicant Cindy Li was present. Board Member Daninger notes that
  the picket tops are pointy and believes they are not allowed. Hernandez agrees
  point tops on fences are not allowed. The applicant notes that they are trying to
  match the neighbor’s fence style which is pointed tops. The applicant also noted
  that the planners only asked for a 3rd horizontal rail be added to provide more
  articulation which the applicant is in agreement. Kuchenski asks the applicant if
  the spare tops are important to the design or could the top be squared off. The
  applicant responses that the fence was already ordered it. Tsai asks if the fence still
  meets fire department access requirements. The applicant response yes, the gates
  will remain open during normal business hours with a knox box for fire department
  access. Udani notes that the applicant should always wait to get approval by the
  city before ordering materials. Hernandez propose a solution to add the 3rd rail be
  added to the top and square off the fence.

MOTION:

  •  Daninger makes a motion to approve the application with the following
  conditions: 1) The applicant shall revise the fence design to show and place the
  3rd horizontal railing above of the spear tops, which will avoid the notion of any
  points or ornamentation along its tops; and 2) The applicant shall resubmit a
  revised set of drawings for the City Architect to verify and approve.
  •  The second was by Chairmen Udani.
  •  The motion carried with the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Udani, Hernandez, Tsai, Daninger, Ng
  Noes:  None

ITEM 7:  438 North Hidalgo Avenue

  •  This is an application for eight (8) window replacements, three (3) new windows,
  re-design of the front porch, and new rear landing on an existing 2-story single-
  family residence.
  •  Applicant: Alison Fung and Kaizen Chen
  •  Recommended Action: APPROVAL WITH CONDITIONS - The proposed project
  is approved with conditions of approval.
  •  Discussion: The applicant was present. The applicant provides an opening
  statement that notes the design intent is to find ways to make simple changes
  and to match a similar architectural style to the original. Board Member Ng asked
  if the balcony doors could have horizontal mullions to match the existing doors.

  4
   The applicant agrees and is ok to add those on the doors to match. Ng asked if
  the door style shown in the elevation drawings is the proposed door design. The
  applicant responded yes and notes that the owner wants a traditional Spanish
  style door. Ng notes that the proposed pillars are not an improvement to the
  overall front yard design and questions if they should be removed from the scope
  of work. The applicant notes that the proposed pillar will be in complementary to
  a future phase where new raised planters will be located at the front of the
  house. Vice Chair Hernandez asked if the proposed color for the wood is to be
  blue. The applicant states it is to match the existing, or similar. Chairman Udani
  asked if the proposed stairs are to maintain the red color to match existing. Board
  Member Daninger notes that keynote #3 for the proposed door states the existing
  door to remain and not to change. Daninger recommends changing this to show
  a new door with further details. The applicant notes that the material board was
  not presented as part of the agenda. The board highlights that their decision
  needs to be only based on the information provided in the agenda packet,
  therefore any other material presented will be for clarification only in response to
  the board member’s question. Staff presented the material board as provided by
  the applicant to the board members. Hernandez notes that materials and color
  shown as part of the agenda packet will be approved, and if changes to it are
  desired, then the applicant must return to the board to present an accurate and
  consistent set of drawings. Board member Daninger notes that the final packet
  needs to be corrected throughout, such as the inconsistency of what is existing
  and what is proposed.

MOTION:

  •  Hernandez makes a motion to approve the application with the following
  conditions: 1) Remove from scope of work and the plan set the proposed pillars;
  2) Revise scope of work to include all window and door work, including
  window/door replacements, window/door removals, and new windows/doors; 3)
  Revise the drawings to accurately show what is existing to remain and what is
  the new proposed items; 4) Revise front door color and style to be more
  compatible with the existing Spanish style; 5) Provide horizontal grids to the
  proposed glazed balcony doors to be consistent with the existing window and
  door grid system; 6) The applicant shall clearly identify the proposed color of
  wood elements including, but not limited to, window frame, window trim, wood
  railing, and wood rafters on the plans; and 7) The applicant shall resubmit a
  revised set of drawings for the City Architect to verify and approve.
  •  The second was by Board Member Ng.
  •  The motion carried with the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Udani, Hernandez, Tsai, Daninger, Ng
  Noes:  None

ITEM 8:  625 South Palm Avenue

  •  This is an application for two (2) new free-standing steel solar carport / canopy
  structures for an existing parking lot on a commercial warehouse property.
  •  Applicant: Tammy Trodden and Tom Djokovich
  •  Recommended Action: APPROVAL WITH CONDITIONS - The proposed project
  is approved with conditions of approval.

  5
   •  Discussion: The applicants were present, including a representative from Solar
  Energy Builders. The applicant noted that the plans in the agenda does show the
  graphically the location of the columns. Kuchenski asks if Planning has reviewed
  the project in terms of parking stall width next to columns. Staff answers yes, the
  planners have reviewed this project prior to Design Review. Kuchenski asked the
  applicant where the placement is of the electrical disconnect mounted on the
  columns. The applicant notes that disconnect will be facing away from the street.
  Tsai asks if the proposed height is a standard height or was the height determined
  due to fire department clearance. The applicant notes the height was dictated by
  sufficient for solar gain and the fire department requirements of minimum height of
  14 foot 6 inches at the lowest point.

MOTION:

  •  Hernandez makes a motion to approve the application without conditions.
  •  The second was by Board Member Ng.
  •  The motion carried with the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Udani, Hernandez, Tsai, Daninger, Ng
  Noes:  None

ITEM 9:  2415 Whitney Drive

  •  This is an application for 530 SF second-story addition to the existing 1-story
  single-family residence, including a new covered front porch and covered balcony
  facing the rear.
  •  Applicant: King Choi & Benjuro Thomas
  •  Recommended Action: APPROVAL WITH CONDITIONS - The proposed project
  is approved with conditions of approval.
  •  Discussion: The applicants were present. Board Member Ng notes that the fence
  should be part of the design review. Staff agrees and asks the board members to
  also review the proposed fencing and walls in the project. Ng and Daninger both
  noted the drawing layout is confusing due to the combination of proposed ADU
  drawings and proposed addition. Ng notes that the proposed side rolling gate is a
  solid wrought iron panel and does not match the other fencing materials. Staff
  notes that there are two proposed fencing styles, one with a solid panel and one
  with vertical rails. Hernandez mentioned that the solid fence is acceptable along
  the side yard facing Carlos Street to provide a level of privacy. The applicant
  notes that Planning asked for the rolling gate to be setback from the property line
  due to vehicle access clear of the public street. Ng asks there needs to be a focal
  arched window at the first floor along the East elevation facing Whitney drive to
  align with the Spanish style. Udani also notes that the proposed wood fence is
  out of place and does not align with the Spanish style. Ng notes there should be
  an arched front door to match with the arched porch entry and the attic vent
  should be more of a Spanish style. The applicant agrees that the proposed
  fencing can be updated to a wrought iron fence as requested. Ng notes the 2nd
  floor portion of the porch roof is exaggerated and too modern. Tsai agrees that it
  is too high. Hernandez notes that roof tiles are not shown in elevation even
  though it is called out. Ng and Udani emphasize that no wood fences should be
  proposed. Ng notes that it is strange for no window to be proposed in front of the
  sink and asks that the applicant revisit the kitchen layout or to propose a window

  6
   in front of the sink. Staff notes that many of these changes were asked of the
  applicant in the previous correction letter.

MOTION:

  •  Ng makes a motion to approve the application with the following conditions: 1)
  The applicant shall provide an alternative material finish for the proposed porch
  base and steps, such as brick, stone, or stucco wall with a tile flooring, to better
  match the proposed Spanish Revival architecture style; 2) Revise proposed site
  plan to clearly identify where the various fencing types occur along Carlos Street
  and Whitney Drive; 3) Revise roofing material to a true Spanish clay tile or similar
  to better align with the architectural style; 4) Reduce the scale of the porch gable
  to provide better balance at the front entry and re-locate the center window to the
  back wall; 5) Revise the north gable roof to be proportional and symmetrical with
  respect to the front elevation facing Whitney Drive; 6) Revise the wood fencing
  material to a decorative wrought iron fence type; 7) The applicant shall clarify the
  proposed kitchen floor plan layout; 8) Revise the attic vent style to be round in
  shape that aligns with the Spanish style; 9) The applicant shall specify the color
  and material of the proposed window frame and trim; and 10) The applicant shall
  resubmit a revised set of drawings for the City Architect to verify and approve.
  •  The second was by Board Member Daninger.
  •  The motion carried with the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Udani, Hernandez, Tsai, Daninger, Ng
  Noes:  None

ITEM 10:  69 East Main Street

  •  This is an application for exterior and site improvements, for business known as
  “Dollar Tree”, to an existing 14,525 SF commercial property, including exterior
  façade refurbishing, two (2) new canopies, new storefront, new signage, new wall
  display, lighting, and public street furniture.
  •  Applicant: Steven Schechter
  •  Recommended Action: APPROVAL WITH CONDITIONS - The proposed project
  is approved with conditions of approval.
  •  Discussion: The applicants were present. Board Member Udani asked the
  intention behind the wall mounted artwork. The applicant responded that the
  applicant will be working with the city on the artwork that will be presented on the
  wall mounted displays. Ng noted that the decal needs to be of high-quality to
  avoid fading or deterioration over a short period of time. The applicant made note
  of this comment and plans to provide a more durable product. Hernandez asked
  if there was a sign program discussed in a previous DRB meeting or in place.
  Staff responded there is a sign program that was approved previously. Staff
  mentioned the exception only in what was presented today is the southeast
  corner sign is different because it provides lettering which the approve signage
  did not have. Hernandez notes that the signs on the south and east elevation are
  not similar in size to the corner sign. Hernandez would like to for the signage to
  have the lettering return color to be white and for them to match in size and
  scale. Hernandez wants to see the size in between both sizes, so finding a
  medium of the two sizes. Ng mentions that the larger signs on the south and east

  7
   elevations should fit in between the lighter horizontal brick colors. In response to
  the applicant questions about the 6 foot clearance along Stoneman is possible,
  Staff did go out on site to ensure 6 foot clear is achievable with the proposed
  planter. Ng notes that the bike rack is missed placed since there is no entrance
  near there. Daninger agrees and notes the bike rack needs to be closer to the
  bike rack. Hernandez asks the applicant the intention behind the location of the
  proposed planter. The applicant response the intention was to center it in
  between the façade transitions and complement the overall design. Ng agrees
  that the planters break up the massive wall and the City’s push for more greenery
  and landscaping. Ng and Daninger notes that the concrete bench used to be a
  base for the magazine boxes. Hernandez states the bike racks needs to be
  relocated near the main entrance. Ng asks if the graphics are place holders or
  the proposed graphics for review. The applicant responses that the graphics are
  placeholder to be reviewed in the future by City staff. The applicant asks to clarify
  if the planter does not meet clearance what is the alternative direction for this
  side of the building. Staff responded that the applicant shall verify the clearance
  first then adjust the planter length and width as need to maintain landscaping
  along Stoneman.

MOTION:

  •  Ng makes a motion to approve the application with the following conditions: 1)
  The applicant shall remove sidewalk furniture including chairs, table, and
  umbrella from the project, with the exception of the proposed fixed bench, since
  this furniture may risk non-compliance with accessibility clearance in the public
  right-of-way and the City’s desire to maintain wide unobstructed sidewalks in this
  high pedestrian traffic area; 2) The applicant must show location and dimensions
  of existing street trees along South Stoneman Avenue. Ensure a minimum of 6-
  foot clearance is maintained along the sidewalk, particularly where the proposed
  planter area is located; 3) Ensure that the decorative/art features will not be used
  for advertisements at any point; 4) Ensure the related approved signage program
  and/or plans are compatible with the approved design determined during this
  November 14, 2023 DRB meeting; 5) The applicant shall re-locate the proposed
  bike rack closer to the primary entrance, while maintaining accessibility clearance
  requirements; 6) The applicant shall select a high-quality and durable product for
  the proposed window decal; 7) The applicant shall work with City Staff on
  determining how the proposed planter is to be maintained, irrigated, and
  sustained at a high-quality; 8) The applicant shall resubmit a revised set of
  drawings for the City Architect to verify and approve.
  •  The second was by Board Member Hernandez.
  •  The motion carried with the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Udani, Hernandez, Tsai, Daninger, Ng
  Noes:  None

  8
 F. ADJOURNMENT:

  •  We will adjourn to the next meeting on November 28, 2023.

MOTION:

  •  Board Member Hernandez moved to adjourn the meeting at 10:53 P.M.
  •  The second was by Board Member Daninger.
  •  The motion carried with the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Udani, Hernandez, Tsai, Daninger, Ng
  Noes:  None

ATTEST:

_____________________
Steve Kuchenski
Secretary
